newsitem.title: USA: Warmer, clear harvest weather seen for US Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Warmer, clear harvest weather seen for US Midwest.

text.p: Following a cold weekend, forecasts call for warmer, dry weather throughout the U.S. Midwest next week that should allow farmers to harvest much of the remaining corn and soybeans, meteorologists said.
"There should be a lot of harvesting," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.
Cattle also should benefit from the weather, with mostly dry, warmer conditions forecast for the High Plains next week, meteorologists said.

Cold should precede next week's warm weather, with Friday and Saturday temperatures averaging 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal, said Solberg. Lows from the teens to low 20s were forecast for the Midwest overnight Friday and early Saturday and 20s in the northern Plains to about 32 degrees in the Texas Panhandle.

Temperatures should then rise with highs in the 50s and 60s across the Midwest early next week, with readings likely reaching into the 60s in the northern Plains and 70s in the southern Plains, forecasters said.
Other than a chance of light showers Tuesday, the Midwest should be dry until Nov 9 and 10, said Tim Bowden, Weather Express Inc meteorologist.
